sentences.text:
2. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and learned HCGP for respondent No.1/State and perused the material on record.
3.

Charge sheet has been filed against the appellant for offences punishable under Sections 363,
376(3) of IPC and Section 3(1)(w), 3(2)(v) of SC/ST (POA) Amendment Act, 2015.
4. Case in Crime No.69/2022 was registered at Chikkaballapura Women Police Station under Section 363 of IPC against the appellant herein on a complaint lodged by the mother of the victim.
In the said complaint it is alleged that the victim girl is aged about 16 years and she was studying in I PUC at Junior College, Chikkaballapura.
On 13.06.2022 at about 9.00 am, she went to College as usual but did not return home in the evening.
Therefore, the complainant and others searched for her in the village and enquired with the relatives and friends, but she was not traced.
Suspecting that the appellant might have kidnapped her, the complaint was lodged.

sentences.text:
The victim girl was traced on 11.07.2022 and her statement was recorded under Section 161 and Section 164 of Cr.P.C.
6.

The learned counsel for the appellant would contend that from the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 of Cr.p.C, it can be seen that it is a clear case of love affair and the victim voluntarily went with the appellant and stayed along with him.
He would contend that there is no force or threat by the appellant and therefore, there is no question of appellant kidnapping the victim.

He further contends that since there was threat by the family members of the victim, the victim went to the village of the appellant on 13.06.2022 and refused to return to her house and therefore, the appellant took her to Chintamani and stayed there, only with an intention that she was not harmed by her parents or other relatives.
He submits that there are no criminal antecedents against the appellant and therefore, he may be enlarged on bail by imposing any conditions.

7. Learned HCGP has opposed the prayer contending that the victim is a minor and she has clearly stated that she was taken by the appellant to Chintamani, wherein they stayed together for four days and again took her to Bangalore, wherein he has committed penetrative sexual assault on her.
He therefore, contends that there is prima facie case against the appellant and accordingly, seeks to reject the petition.
8. According to the prosecution, the date of birth of the victim is 21.05.2006.
Hence, she was aged about 16 years as on the date of commission of the offence.
Her statement was recorded under Section 161 of Cr.p.C. as well as Section 164 of Cr.P.C, which indicate that there was penetrative sexual assault committed against her by the appellant.
The learned counsel for the appellant has disputed the age of the victim, contending that the prosecution has not collected any authentic document to show the correct age of the victim.
However, considering the material on record and since the victim's evidence is not yet recorded, at this Stage, this is not a fit case to enlarge the appellant on bail.
There are chances of influencing or threatening the victim in the event of grant of bail to the appellant.

9. The learned Special Judge is directed to record the victim's evidence as expeditiously as possible,
keeping in view the relevant provisions of the POCSO Act.
Appellant is permitted to file a fresh petition before the special court once the evidence of the victim girl is recorded.
If any such application is filed, the learned Sessions Judge shall dispose of the same without being influenced by any of the observations made herein.
Appeal is dismissed.
